en.name: Basilica of the Sacred Heart (Sacré-Cœur)
en.summary: The white-domed basilica crowning Montmartre, built as a national act of penance after the Franco-Prussian War.
en.body: The Basilica of the Sacré-Cœur was built atop the Montmartre hill following France's defeat in the 1870-71 Franco-Prussian War and the upheaval of the Paris Commune, conceived as a national offering of penance and hope dedicated to the Sacred Heart of Jesus. Constructed largely by public subscription between 1875 and 1914, its distinctive white travertine stone and Romano-Byzantine domes make it one of the most recognisable landmarks on the Paris skyline, with sweeping views across the city from its steps.
